reuse.why: Introduces getDateWithWeekendRule and isWeekendOrHoliday and routes the move rule through them, but the daily-skip rule is not part of the shared definition, so each consumer re-implements it.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend => drop weekend/holiday occurrences' rule is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template, and the holidays Set is rebuilt in four places.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday primitives live in shared/schedules.ts, but the frequency-dependent part of the rule is decided at the server call sites (app.ts handlers, budget template).

scope.why: Changes stay within schedule date logic, the new handler, types and tests; the rule-utils data additions are needed to carry frequency and holidays.

maintainability.why: A future change to how daily schedules or holidays are treated has to be repeated in four differently shaped branches, and schedule-template passes skipWeekend into a helper while also guarding on it outside.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (own daily-skip loops with isWeekendOrHoliday), server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList (own skipWeekend && !isDaily ternary around getDateWithWeekendRule)

disguised_duplication.where: the daily-skip rule appears as a findWeekdayOccurrence closure in getNextDate, a push loop in getUpcomingDates, a continue branch in getDatesInRange and a noSkipWeekend toggle in schedule-template

abstraction_drift.where: holidays added to getDateWithSkippedWeekend and getDateWithWeekendRule; a daily special-case branch added inside shared getNextDate; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template decide the daily rule themselves
